problem: Repeated unrelated main movement invalidated already-running admission and exact-head CI because Writer-Lease-Main-Epoch was required to equal current main before expensive CI, causing repeated sync/retest cycles and delivery starvation.
rootCause: The terminal landing invariant was enforced too early. Admission coupled a candidate's writer lease to a moving global main epoch even though safety only requires exact current-main binding at the serialized terminal landing boundary.
prevention: Admission binds canonical identity to obligation + exact candidate head and validates Writer-Lease-Main-Epoch syntax, but does not fail only because current main advanced after the candidate started.
Writer lease admission validates owner, scope, obligation and exact candidate head while treating observed main movement as non-terminal context.

Terminal merge remains fail-closed: current Writer-Lease-Main-Epoch must equal current main, validated head must equal candidate head, behind_by must be 0, mergeability must be true and required checks must be green.
Unrelated parallel main movement must not restart expensive CI by itself; reconcile only at the landing boundary or earlier when changed-path/conflict-contract impact requires it.
Repeated rebase/retest loops for an unchanged obligation are a starvation signal and should trigger this prevention rule.
outcome: Pending protected merge and production/readback proof.
